subject: Computer Networking
title: Service Mesh for Microservices
description: Learn Service Mesh for Microservices in one minute.

hook.text: Microservices talk over the network. A service mesh manages that traffic without changing app code.

buildup.text: A sidecar proxy sits next to each service. It handles routing, load balancing, retries, and encryption.

discovery.text: Istio and Linkerd add observability: every request shows latency and error rates between services.

twist.text: Sidecars add latency and resource overhead. Each service needs its own proxy. At scale, it adds up.

climax.text: Ambient mesh moves proxy logic to shared nodes. Same benefits, less overhead. Sidecars optional.

punchline.text: A service mesh adds networking superpowers between microservices.

quiz.question: What does a sidecar proxy in a service mesh do?
options: Handles routing, load balancing, and encryption for a service transparently
Stores database records for the service
Compiles the service's source code before deployment

details.summary: A service mesh provides a dedicated infrastructure layer for managing communication between microservices. Sidecar proxies handle traffic routing, load balancing, encryption, observability, and retry logic transparently, removing these concerns from application code.
details.whyItMatters: Microservice architectures create complex service-to-service communication. A service mesh provides consistent networking behavior across all services without requiring each team to implement it.
takeaways: Sidecar proxies handle all inter-service communication transparently
mTLS encrypts traffic between every service automatically
Observability features provide detailed traffic metrics and tracing

faq.question: What problems does a service mesh solve?
faq.answer: Service meshes handle service discovery, load balancing, circuit breaking, retries, timeouts, mutual TLS, traffic splitting for canary deployments, and distributed tracing.

faq.question: When is a service mesh overkill?
faq.answer: For small deployments with fewer than 10 to 20 services, a service mesh adds complexity without proportional benefit. Simple applications with straightforward communication patterns may not need the advanced routing and observability features.
